extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians preparing/submitting manuscripts to the Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and evaluative standards for authors submitting research articles to the Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society, covering scope, file and metadata requirements, ethical and data policies, and the submission/revision workflow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial evaluation criteria (novelty, innovation, significance, advancement)
rubrics_metrics.description: When evaluating papers, the Editorial Board considers a number of criteria such as novelty, innovation, significance, and advancement of the field of research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The journal publishes articles of the highest quality and significance across a broad range of mathematics; submit work that makes a clear, significant advance rather than minor incremental improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unsuitability: too specialised or incremental work
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers which are too specialised or which represent incremental advance within a narrow area should instead be submitted to a more specialist journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such submissions will most probably be rejected by the editors; authors may consider the Proceedings' sister publications for more specialised work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motivating introduction accessible to non-specialists
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles (and sister publications) expect a motivating introduction which sets the work in context and can be understood and appreciated by researchers outside the immediate specialism of the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write an introduction that explains subject and relevance to the wider mathematical community, so editors and readers outside the narrow specialty can appreciate the contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article length policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers submitted to this journal can be of any length. Papers should be as long as is necessary to present the mathematical work they contain clearly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not artificially shorten papers; the journal does not apply higher standards to longer papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with LMS Ethical Policy
rubrics_metrics.description: By submitting to the Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society, authors are confirming that they accept and will abide by the Ethical Policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the LMS Ethical Policy for guidance on expected behaviour of authors, reviewers, and editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preprints and theses policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The LMS will consider papers that have been deposited in preprint or manuscript form on servers such as the arXiv or included as part of a thesis which has not been formally published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author must be able to sign a Licence to Publish granting the LMS the rights to publish the paper (see 'Articles accepted by the Proceedings').

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission system and process
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit articles using the online submission system EditFlow which manages submissions and peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the system's submission form and follow on-screen instructions; links provided on the journal site.

rubrics_metrics.name: File format and source retention
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should submit their paper electronically as a single PDF file. Authors must keep the .tex file that precisely corresponds to the PDF version that they submit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the paper is accepted, the journal will require that particular version of the .tex file. Do not send the .tex file at submission time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code and data availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Any code or data which is necessary to fully evaluate the basis for a paper’s results must either be deposited in a repository prior to submission or submitted with the research article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the Society's Data Access Policy and the LMS policy on Computer Aided Proofs for more information; provide access to reproduce/verify results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Footnote usage
rubrics_metrics.description: The Society discourages the use of footnotes in papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such notes should either be included in the main text in parentheses or included as a formal 'Remark'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choosing a handling editor
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should identify which member of the Editorial Board they would like to handle the paper, choosing the editor whose mathematical interests are closest to that of the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A full list of editors and their field of expertise is available; the Editorial Board may re-assign submissions when appropriate, e.g., for conflicts of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover letter and notes to editor usage
rubrics_metrics.description: On the submission form there are two optional fields: 'Cover Letter' and 'Notes to Editor'. Cover letters will be visible to both editors and any potential reviewers; 'Notes for Editor' will only be seen by editors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cover letters should provide brief context and explain subject and relevance. Include any messages authors do not wish reviewers to see in 'Notes for Editor'. Be respectful and explicitly state any relationships which may create a conflict of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: ORCID iD for corresponding author
rubrics_metrics.description: Corresponding Authors are asked to provide their ORCID iD as part of the submission process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors without an ORCID iD can register via ORCID; registering takes only a few minutes but authors are recommended to complete their ORCID record with their publication history.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required submission metadata
rubrics_metrics.description: The Corresponding Author will be asked to provide the following information: the PDF file, number of authors, full names and email addresses of all authors, title of the paper, MSC subject codes, chosen Editor to handle the paper, confirmation that an abstract is included in the article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure all required fields are completed accurately during submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy and data protection consent
rubrics_metrics.description: When submitting a paper, authors must agree to allow the LMS to store their personal data and will have been informed of the LMS’s data protection policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under UK law the LMS explains how personal data stored on its system will be subsequently used; see the submission portal Privacy Policy for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-submission tracking and withdrawal
rubrics_metrics.description: The Corresponding Author will receive a confirmation email including a link to a manuscript tracking page. This page includes a record of all correspondence, submission files and the paper’s current status and can be used to withdraw the current submission if necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you do not receive the link, contact lmsjournal@lms.ac.uk and cite your paper ID.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revisions and resubmission policy
rubrics_metrics.description: During peer review, editors may ask the author to revise their paper. The email asking for a revised version will contain a link to submit the revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should not submit a revision as a new article. Do not upload a new version of the same paper before a decision on the first version is sent, particularly if the changes are minor. If a letter firmly rejects the paper and does not mention that a resubmission would be considered, the journal will not consider this submission further.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact and recordkeeping
rubrics_metrics.description: If authors have queries they should contact lmsjournals@lms.ac.uk. Authors should take care to keep a copy of all emails sent to any editors, managing editors and LMS publications staff for their own records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite your paper ID in correspondence and retain correspondence records for reference.
